titles.li: The shrine's flame by the road

texts.li: Two of {FACTION}'s fellowship have stopped on the colony's land with a cart of poles and bedrolls. With so many on the roads this year, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, travellers need somewhere to sleep, and they would raise a hostel {PLACE} for a fortnight: a long hut of bedrolls, the shrine's flame and a bread table for anyone at peace who passes.

[ws:faith] With {SITUATION} filling every road, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to raise a hostel {PLACE}. Anyone at peace may sleep there a night or two, {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef}; they would only ask the colony for bread in the mornings, and invite its people to the blessing in the evenings.

[lowtech] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have begun cutting poles {PLACE} for a long hut. {X_nameDef}, who blessed every door on the road behind {X_objective}, open or shut, told {A_nameDef} it would be a hostel for the travellers of the pilgrimage, with the shrine's flame lit at its door.

[!lowtech] A wagon of {FACTION}'s fellowship has pulled off the road {PLACE}, loaded with folding cots and a brass lamp. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they would keep a hostel there for the pilgrims and travellers of the road, a fortnight or so, and asked only for bread.

[their:grateful] The pilgrim fellowship remembers the colony's welcome, and {X_nameDef} has chosen its land for their hostel this year, {PLACE}, so the region's travellers sleep under the colony's eye.

settled.li: The hostel stands {PLACE}: a long hut with bedrolls in a row, the shrine's flame burning at its door, and a bread table under an awning where anyone at peace may sit.
{FACTION}'s hostel is up {PLACE}, and the shrine's flame has been lit; {X_nameDef} says it won't go out until they leave.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the hostel has watched the colony's people come to the evening blessing night after night, and asks whether the colony could use someone who keeps a door open for strangers.

farewell.li: [faces] The hostel's fellowship blessed every door of the colony as they left, open or shut, and left their long hut standing as a shelter for the road. {GUESTS} travellers slept there while they kept it.
[faces] {X_nameDef} put out the shrine's flame at dawn and walked on with the last of the pilgrims, leaving the hut for whoever needs it next. The region's faces passed through it, {GUESTS} of them.
The fellowship's hostel is empty, its flame out, its hut left standing by the road. {X_nameDef} blessed the gate on the way past.

lines.li: A shell for every shrine, and a bed for every walker.
Bless this door, open or shut.
Who's sleeping in the end bed tonight?
The flame stays lit until we go.
[evening] The blessing's at dusk, and everyone's welcome.

momentLines.li: [quarrel] Keep that quarrel off the road, both of you.
[gift] Leave the hut for the next walker.

helpTexts.li: [medicine] {X_nameDef} brought the colony a bundle of healing herbs the travellers had left in thanks for their beds: {THING}.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat at the hostel's bread table while the travellers traded news of every town on the road, and came back knowing who was feuding with whom.

li.label: Send bread to the hostel each morning
li.tip: One of the colony carries food out to the hostel's table every morning while it stands: meals when the colony has them, else raw food. The fellowship blesses the colony for it.

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the pilgrims' hostel has come to the gate with an empty basket. There are more travellers on the road than the fellowship can feed, {X_pronoun} says, and asks whether the colony would send bread to the hostel's table each morning while it stands.
The hostel's bread table was bare this morning, and {X_nameDef} has come to ask the colony, humbly, for bread each morning for the travellers while the hostel stands.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} thanks the colony anyway and goes back to bake what the fellowship can.

outcomes.li: The colony will send bread to the hostel each morning, and the first basket is already on its way.

li.label: Go to the evening blessing
li.tip: Whoever is free goes over to the hostel at dusk, where the fellowship blesses the travellers and the colony together. Recreation and a little peace; the crowded hut has its cough going round.

outcomes.li: The colony is going over to the hostel for the evening blessing, where the shrine's flame is already lit.
Whoever isn't working is walking over to the hostel for the blessing, and the travellers have made room on the benches.

li.label: the evening blessing at the hostel

titles.li: A lantern at the edge of the land

texts.li: Lantern Wardens of {FACTION} are making camp {PLACE}, three of them and two hounds, because {BEAST} is on the colony's land. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they will light the lantern every night and follow its trail by day until it falls, or ten days.

[lowtech] Three Wardens of {FACTION} with boar-spears and two lean hounds are making camp {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that where a lantern burns, someone was taken, and {BEAST} is out there.

settled.li: The Wardens' post is up {PLACE}: a fire, three bedrolls, the hounds tied by the woodpile and the lantern on its pole, ready for dark.
The lantern post stands {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} has opened the Wardens' book at {BEAST}'s page.

farewell.li: [together] The Wardens put out their lantern at dawn and wrote {BEAST}'s page with the colony's name in it, a red cord knotted beside it. Then they took the road home with their hounds.
[fell] {BEAST} has fallen, and the Wardens' lantern went out with it. {X_nameDef} wrote the page at the fire before they packed up, and the hounds were the first down the road.
[cold] The trail went cold, and the Wardens took down their post. {X_nameDef} left {BEAST}'s page open in the book and promised to light the lantern again if it comes back.
[hound] The Wardens packed up their post one hound short. {X_nameDef} said the other would follow the road home when it was ready, and didn't sound sure.
The Wardens' lantern post is empty, its lantern down off its pole and the fire raked out.

lines.li: Where a lantern burns, someone was taken.
Keep the hounds fed and the lantern trimmed.
It came down to the water at dawn, the tracks say so.
A beast that takes a person answers for it.
Eleven years Garrow waited by his lantern.
[night] Light it, and keep it lit.

momentLines.li: [lantern] Light the lantern, it's getting dark.
[lantern] The lantern is lit, and the page stays open.
[warn] It's close to your walls, keep your people in.
[warn] The hounds have its scent, and it's coming your way.
[track] Fresh sign by the trees, it passed here at dawn.
[track] Quiet now, it's just over the rise.
[trail] Your shot and our spears, and we'll close the page today.

helpTexts.li: [tales] {A_nameDef} sat up at the Wardens' lantern while {X_nameDef} told of Tobin Garrow and the eleven years at the crossroads, and of every red cord in the book.

li.label: Give them meat for the hounds
li.tip: One of the colony carries raw meat out to the Wardens' post for their hounds.

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the Wardens' post has come to the gate with the hounds at {X_possessive} heels. The trail is long and the hounds are thin, {X_pronoun} says, and asks for some of the colony's meat for them.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} nods and says the hounds will hunt for themselves, then.

outcomes.li: Meat is going out to the Wardens' post, and the hounds are already at the edge of it, waiting.

li.label: Send our best shot on the trail with them
li.tip: The colony's best shot goes after the beast with two of the Wardens: a place in the hunt, and a lesson in tracking. If it falls, one of them skins it where it lies, the hide for their book and the meat for the colony.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} has gone out on the trail with two of the Wardens and a hound, after {BEAST}.

li.label: Sit up at the lantern with them
li.tip: Whoever is free goes over to the Wardens' fire at dusk to sit up by the lantern and hear the book read. Recreation; the Wardens warm to the colony.

outcomes.li: The colony is going over to sit up at the Wardens' lantern tonight, and {X_nameDef} has the book open on {X_possessive} knees.

li.label: an evening at the Wardens' lantern

texts.li: Two fellows of {FACTION} have pitched a small camp {PLACE}, beside {OLDPLACE}, to measure it. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they would say exactly what lies inside before they go.

settled.li: The scholars' camp is up beside {OLDPLACE}: two tents, a fire and a table of instruments, and a chain already pegged out along the old walls.

farewell.li: [opened] The scholars broke into {OLDPLACE} as they went, and whatever slept there is awake now. {X_nameDef} called it the price of knowing.
[measured] The scholars packed their instruments and left their notes on {OLDPLACE} with the colony: {READING}.
The scholars' camp by {OLDPLACE} is empty, its pegs pulled and its fire out.

lines.li: Hold the chain straight, I'll read it.
Strictly speaking, that is two questions.
Write it down before you forget it.

momentLines.li: [measure] Forty paces, and the wall still going.
[measure] The stone sounds hollow here, write that down.
[read] Here is what lies inside, as exactly as we can say it.
